summary: The note describes the rapid growth of outdoor "green exercise" in a city from September 2023 into the New Year. It covers park fitness equipment, new forest trails, outdoor class programs, school curriculum changes, supporting apps, winter sports, and a city council plan to expand green spaces. Local residents and experts credit the trend with community, mental health, and fitness benefits.
one_line: A local city's green exercise trend grew from September 2023 through January through parks, trails, classes, schools, apps, winter sports, and city support.
key_facts: Fitness expert Jenna McTavish spoke about the appeal of outdoor workouts on September 5, 2023, at the "Fresh Fitness Fiesta" event at City Park.

Starting mid-September, local groups introduced free-to-use fitness equipment in Cedar Grove Park, such as resistance bands and yoga mats, with Pilates, yoga, and calisthenics led by local fitness professionals.
George Atkinson, an avid yoga practitioner, said on September 22nd that "Every day, more people join in" at Cedar Grove Park.
The city's Department of Recreation and Parks inaugurated several new trails in Grandwood Forest on October 6th, with markers about local flora and fauna.
Miriam Lopez, a 33-year-old hiker and local teacher, described the trails as "a gym with a living, breathing heart."
A calendar of outdoor fitness classes, from "Bootcamp at Dawn" to "Twilight Tai Chi," became available on November 12th, established by local fitness entrepreneur Dave Hollister.

On November 20th, local schools added outdoor activities such as orienteering and environmental conservation projects to physical education classes; teacher Mark Reynolds praised the impact on students.
By late November 2023, new apps offering trail maps, workout tracking, and virtual communities supported outdoor exercisers; runner Sarah Kim praised them.
The local Snow and Ice Festival began December 11th with workshops introducing cross-country skiing and snowshoeing; 42-year-old Derek Sands is a snowshoe enthusiast.
The city council announced plans to expand green spaces and outdoor fitness resources.
The "New Year, True You" outdoor fitness challenge kicked off on January 8th, inviting all locals to set healthful intentions.
